fields: goals: awareness, engagement, conversion, event, announcement. formats: post, carousel-cover, poster, banner, thumbnail, story, flyer. evidence: strong (large-sample or controlled data), mixed (data disagrees by context), practice (practitioner convention). Templates are starting shapes; the line that ships names this audience's concrete outcome.
defaults: Cold feeds: a specific number plus a concrete outcome, in sentence case, information-carrying words first. ALL-CAPS headlines and question covers underperformed on carousels; 'how to', 'you' and 'secret/trick' lost clicks in browse (not search) contexts.

headline.name: Number / list
headline.example: 7 pricing mistakes killing your margin
headline.use_when: Educational content, listicles, carousels where each slide is one item. The best-evidenced headline shape; numerals beat words, 3-10 do best.
headline.pitfall: A number the content cannot pay off slide for slide.

headline.name: List teaser
headline.example: 9 onboarding steps most SaaS teams skip (#6 is free)
headline.use_when: A carousel that needs a reason to swipe; the number promises completion and the twist promises payoff.
headline.pitfall: Burying the promised twist in the last slide, past where most people stop.

headline.name: Direct benefit
headline.example: Payroll done in 10 minutes, without spreadsheets
headline.use_when: A product with a measurable result; cold-to-warm conversion.
headline.pitfall: A timeframe or result the product cannot prove.

headline.name: How-to
headline.example: How to price your first course (even with no audience)
headline.use_when: Search- and save-driven education, LinkedIn documents, Pinterest.
headline.pitfall: Weak in pure browse feeds and paid placements; lead with the outcome there instead.

headline.name: Question
headline.example: Still chasing invoices by email?
headline.use_when: The pain is recognisable in one glance.
headline.pitfall: Underperformed as a carousel cover; a yes/no question invites 'no' and a scroll.

headline.name: Bold claim
headline.example: The running shoe that weighs less than your phone.
headline.use_when: Brand campaigns with proof on the asset or right beside it.
headline.pitfall: An unsourced superlative is a legal risk, not just a credibility one.

headline.name: Contrarian
headline.example: Stop posting daily. Post this twice a week instead.
headline.use_when: Expert and thought-leadership audiences who have heard the standard advice.
headline.pitfall: The next slide or subhead must deliver the substance at once, or it reads as bait.

headline.name: Curiosity gap
headline.template: The [one thing] [experts] won't tell you about [topic]
headline.example: The one line every winning proposal has
headline.use_when: Engagement content whose payoff is immediate.
headline.pitfall: An unpaid gap costs trust; avoid 'secret' and 'trick' in paid browse placements.

headline.name: Audience call-out
headline.example: Freelance designers: read this before your next quote.
headline.use_when: Narrow targeting where self-identification does the filtering.
headline.pitfall: Personal-attribute call-outs ('Are you overweight?') break Meta ad policy.

headline.name: Urgency
headline.example: Early-bird pricing ends Friday 14 March.
headline.use_when: A real deadline, late in the funnel.
headline.pitfall: A fake deadline is deceptive advertising (FTC); never invent one.

headline.name: Scarcity
headline.example: Only 12 workshop seats left.
headline.use_when: Genuinely limited inventory, stated as an exact number.
headline.pitfall: Invented scarcity is a legal risk.

headline.name: Social proof / stat
headline.example: 73% of SaaS homepages fail this test
headline.use_when: Credibility, B2B, LinkedIn; pairs with the data-as-hero visual hook.
headline.pitfall: The stat needs a source on the asset or in the caption.

headline.name: Before / after
headline.example: From 40 tabs to one dashboard in a week.
headline.use_when: A visible transformation; pairs with the before-after split visual hook. Two-slide carousels are their own genre.
headline.pitfall: Results that are not real are deceptive.

headline.name: Problem-agitate
headline.example: Your inbox is a to-do list someone else writes.
headline.use_when: Pain-aware audiences; the subhead or slide 2 carries the solution.
headline.pitfall: Agitation with no relief line reads as negativity.

headline.name: Pattern interrupt
headline.template: [Surprising word or non-sequitur], then a reframing sub-line.
headline.example: Boring is the new growth hack.
headline.use_when: Saturated feeds and outdoor, where sameness is the enemy.
headline.pitfall: Needs a sub-line that makes sense of it within one glance.

headline.name: Insider
headline.example: What top Etsy shops do differently with photos
headline.use_when: Expertise content for an aspiring audience.
headline.pitfall: Vague 'top performers' with no named source feels made up.

headline.name: Mistake / warning
headline.example: 5 contract mistakes that cost freelancers money
headline.use_when: Loss aversion; negative framing beat positive superlatives in browse data.
headline.pitfall: Fear without a fix; every mistake needs its remedy.

headline.name: Announcement
headline.example: New: invoices that chase themselves.
headline.use_when: Launches and features; lead with the benefit, not just the name.
headline.pitfall: A product name alone tells nobody why to care.

headline.name: Event essentials
headline.template: [Event name]: [weekday date] · [venue, city] + [why attend in 6 words or fewer]
headline.example: Night Market · Sat 14 Mar, 7 pm · Riverside Hall
headline.use_when: Events. What, when, where and how must read at the viewing distance, in that order of size.
headline.pitfall: Ambiguous dates (03/04); include the weekday and the time.

headline.name: Offer first
headline.example: 30% off all plants, this weekend only
headline.use_when: Promotions where the number is the hero.
headline.pitfall: Fine print far from the claim; keep conditions next to the asterisk.

headline.name: Comparison
headline.example: Spreadsheets vs a CRM that updates itself
headline.use_when: Positioning; pairs with split layouts.
headline.pitfall: Naming a competitor invites legal review; compare against a way of working instead.

headline.name: Bracketed clarifier
headline.example: The launch week plan [free template]
headline.use_when: Telling the reader what format they get; brackets lifted CTR in browse data.
headline.pitfall: Promising a template the post does not contain.

visual.name: Scale contrast
visual.device: One element at 3x or more the size of everything else.
visual.works_when: There is one clear hero: product, number or word. Small things blown up look impressive.
visual.backfires_when: Two elements compete at similar size, or something naturally big is shown small.
visual.layout_hint: Hero fills 40-70% of the frame; copy takes the remaining band.
visual.imagery_hint: Macro or close crop of the hero on a clean field.

visual.name: Oversized type as image
visual.device: Type fills 50-80% of the frame and is the picture.
visual.works_when: Announcements, stats, quotes, posters; five words or fewer; a strong heavy face.
visual.backfires_when: A long headline forced big into five lines, or light weights that dissolve at feed size.
visual.layout_hint: Type-only layout; imagery may be skipped.
visual.imagery_hint: None, or a texture behind the type.

visual.name: Face with eye contact
visual.device: A human face looking at the viewer.
visual.works_when: Awareness, personal brands, thumbnails (most breakout thumbnails show a face).
visual.backfires_when: The face pulls every fixation and nobody reads the copy.
visual.layout_hint: Face on a third, copy opposite.
visual.imagery_hint: Expressive close-up whose emotion matches the promise.

visual.name: Directed gaze
visual.device: The person looks or points toward the headline or product.
visual.works_when: You want the face's pull and the copy read; eye-tracking shows more fixations on text and brand.
visual.backfires_when: Gaze points out of frame or at a corner nobody needs.
visual.layout_hint: Subject on one side facing in; headline where the gaze lands.
visual.imagery_hint: Prompt the gaze direction toward the copy zone.

visual.name: Single colour pop
visual.device: Neutral or monochrome frame with one saturated accent on the hero or CTA.
visual.works_when: Isolation effect; the accent marks the one thing to see or do.
visual.backfires_when: The accent appears on three or more elements, fails contrast, or relies on red/green alone.
visual.layout_hint: Accent reserved for the hero or CTA only.
visual.imagery_hint: Desaturated plate; colour added in the composition.

visual.name: Negative space
visual.works_when: Premium brands, posters, minimal products; the one element becomes unmissable.
visual.backfires_when: The subject is illegible at thumbnail size; Google responsive display images cap blank space near 80%.
visual.layout_hint: Subject on a third intersection; copy in the open field.
visual.imagery_hint: Name the empty area physically (smooth warm-grey wall, clear pale sky).

visual.name: Breaking the frame
visual.device: The subject overlaps the border or the type, popping out of a panel.
visual.works_when: Product cutouts; adds depth on flat feeds.
visual.backfires_when: The overlap covers letters of the headline, or the crop cuts the subject at a joint or face.
visual.layout_hint: Cutout layer above the headline layer; keep key letters clear.
visual.imagery_hint: Cutout with alpha plus a plate; matching light direction.

visual.name: Unexpected juxtaposition
visual.device: A visual pun or two things that do not belong together.
visual.works_when: Awareness, outdoor, pattern interrupts; scale and humour.
visual.backfires_when: It takes more than two seconds to decode, or the joke has nothing to do with the product.
visual.layout_hint: The odd pairing is the hero; one short line explains it.
visual.imagery_hint: Describe both objects and their relation precisely.

visual.name: Before / after split
visual.device: Vertical or diagonal split of two states.
visual.works_when: Transformations: products, services, renovations; two-slide carousels.
visual.backfires_when: Results are not real, or both halves are equal so the eye has no entry; make 'after' larger or brighter.
visual.layout_hint: Split layout, labels on each half, 'after' on the reading-order side.
visual.imagery_hint: Two plates with the same camera and light.

visual.name: Implied motion
visual.device: Blur, diagonals, mid-action, splash, motion lines.
visual.backfires_when: It reads as a rendering glitch at small sizes or fights the text.
visual.layout_hint: Diagonal composition; text on the calm side.
visual.imagery_hint: Frozen mid-action, motion blur on the background.

visual.name: Texture / tactile
visual.device: Paper, grain, fabric or macro surfaces.
visual.works_when: Craft, food, beauty, premium; stands out from flat vector feeds.
visual.backfires_when: Busy texture under text kills legibility; heavy grain bloats JPEGs.
visual.layout_hint: Texture under a solid text panel or in the image area only.
visual.imagery_hint: Macro surface with soft raking light.

visual.name: Hands with product
visual.device: Hands holding or using the product.
visual.backfires_when: AI hands with wrong finger counts, or hands hiding the label.
visual.layout_hint: Product near the optical centre, label facing out.
visual.imagery_hint: Use a real product photo cutout; generate the hands and setting only.

visual.name: Data as hero
visual.device: One giant number plus a short label.
visual.works_when: Stats, reports, B2B, LinkedIn; eyes jump to numbers.
visual.backfires_when: The number is unsourced or competes with a second number.
visual.layout_hint: Number at display size; label and source below.

visual.name: Strong silhouette
visual.device: A shape recognisable from its outline.
visual.backfires_when: The shape is ambiguous or figure-ground contrast is low.
visual.layout_hint: Silhouette centred or on a third with generous space.
visual.imagery_hint: Backlit or flat-colour subject on a contrasting field.

visual.name: Lo-fi native
visual.device: Looks like a phone photo, a note or a real screenshot.
visual.works_when: Cold Meta and TikTok traffic; recognition and proof.
visual.backfires_when: It fakes platform UI, buttons or system warnings (Google prohibits them).
visual.imagery_hint: Real screenshots or phone photos over generated ones.

visual.name: Colour-block field
visual.device: A bold flat colour field or geometric blocks.
visual.works_when: Series recognition: the same field on every asset and size.
visual.backfires_when: Low-contrast pastels, or white fields under white platform UI (TikTok, YouTube).
visual.layout_hint: Field as background, type and cutout on top.

carousel.arc: Hook (1) -> why it matters (2) -> one idea per slide (3 to N-2) -> summary (N-1) -> CTA (N). Default 8-12 slides; 13-20 only when every slide earns its swipe; two-slide before/after is a valid genre.

covers.example: 73% of SaaS homepages fail this test

carousel.cover_rules: One promise readable in under 2 seconds, 6-10 words, an honest number, sentence case, not logo-first. It must also work as the 3:4 profile-grid tile.
swipe_cues: arrow or 'Swipe' chip at the right edge inside the margin
an image, line or shape that crosses into the next slide
a cliffhanger sentence resolved on the next slide
an element cut off at the right edge

closers.example: Save this for your next launch
Send this to a teammate who quotes too low
Comment GUIDE and I'll send the template
Follow for a pricing teardown every Tuesday
Book a call: link in bio

carousel.closer_rules: One action that matches the goal. Repeat the cover's look and the brand mark, because Instagram can re-serve a carousel from a later slide. LinkedIn document links do not click in-feed; put URLs in the post text.
